Subject: Questions on VPC platform fee, burst credits and oncall retainer

Hi Logan —

Thanks again for the demo last week. Procurement asked us to get clarity on a couple of commercial items before we move to redlines:

1) Platform fee amortization: your standard SOW shows the platform fee amortized over 12 months. We have a mid-year budget cycle — would you consider a 6-month amortization for a pilot?

2) Burst credits: we expect occasional bursts during nightly batches. Can you confirm how burst credits are consumed vs. platform units? Is there an overage cap?

3) Support/oncall retainer: we need clarity on alerting windows and the cost to add a Level 2 oncall retainer.

I attached a workbook with our expected weekly tokens and a sample runbook for batch jobs. Can your team propose a short matrix (pilot-friendly) that aligns to our budget?

Ellen

Subject: Re: Questions on VPC platform fee, burst credits and oncall retainer

Thanks Ellen — this is exactly the right level of detail. Looping in Kim (pricing lead) and Marissa (customer success / SOW) to propose a concise matrix for a 6-month pilot + handling burst behavior.

Quick thoughts:
- We can carve a pilot amortization to 6 months for pilot customers; typical trade is capped burst credits and an explicit conversion to usage once pilot converts to annual.
- Burst credits are consumed from the burst pool first; when exhausted, requests are throttled to committed capacity or billed as overage at a higher per-token rate. We can add a hard cap to avoid surprise spend.
- Oncall retainer pricing varies by response SLA (4h vs 1h). We typically show a 24/7 L2 retainer as a fixed monthly line item.

Kim / Marissa — can you propose a short table (3 rows) that I can send Ellen tomorrow? Aim to show: platform fee amortization (6m vs 12m), burst credit cap (monthly), overage rate, and optional L2 retainer price + response SLA.

Thanks,
Logan

Ellen, Logan —

Attached is a compact matrix for TiltHealth based on the workbook you shared. TL;DR version inlined below. If this looks acceptable we can put the exact numbers into the SOW and add a clause for conversion at renewal.

-- Compact Commercial Matrix (pilot) --
1) Platform fee amortization: 6-month pilot amortization at 60% of our standard monthly platform fee (applied as a credit in months 1–6). Upon annual conversion, remaining value is reconciled to the annual schedule.
2) Burst credits: 100k burst tokens/month included for pilot. Additional burst consumed billed at 1.75x hosted token rate; hard cap option available at $5k/month (stop-gap).
3) Overage protection: auto-notify at 80% and 95% of burst pool; explicit approval required to enable overage billing.
4) L2 oncall retainer: option A — business-hours L2 retainer at $6k/month (response target 4h). Option B — 24/7 L2 at $18k/month (response target 1h). Both include up to 6 emergency pages/month; additional pages at $250/page.

Attachments: SOW draft will include exact billing rows.

Questions for you, Ellen: do you need the hard cap applied at account-level or per-environment? Also, confirm whether your nightly batches are predictable windowed jobs (we can carve out scheduled bursts from the burst pool).

Kim
Kimberly Park
Pricing Lead, Redwood Inference
kimberly.park@redwood.com
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Ellen Morris <ellen.morris@tilthealth.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 4 Dec 2026 09:32:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Questions on VPC platform fee, burst credits and oncall retainer

Ellen —

Following Kim's matrix, commercial constraints we need to flag:
- We can offer the 6-month amortization pilot at the proposed 60% discount but require a pilot-to-annual conversion clause or a capped conversion fee. This avoids revenue leakage.
- For the hard cap option on burst credits (TiltHealth requested $5k/month), we require a minimum pilot commitment (3 months) and that scheduled batch windows are declared in the SOW so we don't count them against the burst pool.
- Oncall: if you take the 24/7 retainer we can provide an SRE onboarding day (delivery/hand-off) at no additional charge.

If TiltHealth is comfortable with those guardrails I will prepare SOW_TiltHealth_Draft_v1.docx with the pilot tables and signature-ready clauses. Can you confirm preferred cap scope (account vs environment) and if Raj needs legal cc on the SOW?

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference

Logan / Kim / Marissa —

This looks good and pragmatic. A few quick confirmations so legal can prep redlines:

• Hard cap: TiltHealth prefers account-level cap (we have two environments but want a single safety ceiling).
• Scheduled batches: we'll declare our nightly 02:00–04:00 PST window in the SOW — please carve that out from burst consumption.
• Pilot-to-annual conversion: TiltHealth will commit to a 12-month conversion within 60 days of pilot end or pay the agreed conversion fee.

Please proceed with the SOW and DocuSign link when ready. Raj will be cc'd on the SOW review and legal redlines.

Thanks — Ellen
